title: Mandatory prerequisite purchases for all add-on modules
request: For all components and all add-on modules, previous add-on modules must be purchased first. This is not limited to shields; direct high-level purchases must not skip the chain.
precedence: Supersedes earlier direct-upgrade purchase eligibility in navigation/energy/targeting/shield designs. Module prices and actual stats are not changed by this requirement. Standard Basic hull systems remain free where already specified.
purchase_rule: Every module has stable identity and explicit predecessor prerequisites within its component family/feature branch. A shop purchase succeeds only if the required previous module purchases are recorded. Enforce the entire ancestor chain, not merely a display tier or one currently fitted string. Generic Advanced/Elite names across different families are not interchangeable prerequisite IDs.

chains.detail: Basic is standard. To buy Advanced II, Basic II, Intermediate, Intermediate II and Advanced must have been purchased first. If Elite is offered for purchase it requires the full preceding purchase chain; otherwise earned component progression remains its acquisition path. Latest user example uses Intermediate naming; treat Intermediary as a legacy alias, not a second level.
Advanced purchase requires prior Intermediate purchase. Old Advanced/raw2 maps to Intermediate; old Military/raw3 maps to Advanced, preserving stable save/route IDs.
Advanced purchase requires prior Intermediate purchase. Extra/Naval legacy IDs retain their meanings. Standard Basic core is not charged.
All earlier purchasable core modules are required before a later purchase. Basic targeting remains a purchase unless separately made standard by an explicit rule.

Each specialist branch declares its own prerequisite core/module rather than relying on its row position. The previous core module must satisfy the purchase rule; Mining and Salvage remain separate feature branches and neither silently unlocks the other. Any future ranked Mining/Salvage add-ons require the earlier modules of their own branch.

Apply the same prerequisite graph to existing/future drive, laser, scanner, utility, shield-feature, weapon/pylon and other modules wherever ranked add-ons exist. Audit every catalogue entry; no exemption merely because it is outside the named four families. Identical repeatable storage/pylon units retain finite count/capacity and sequential count validation rather than inventing unrelated grade prerequisites.

transaction_and_persistence: Central authoritative runtime purchase validation checks predecessor receipts before charging, changing installation or creating an item. Keyboard, pointer, normal shop, PLUGH, discounted shop and any alternate purchase path use the same validator. A missing prerequisite is not a technology/funds failure.

Persist successful purchases by stable component-family/module ID, independently of current fitted/held equipment. Selling, replacing, removing or transferring a module does not erase that the player purchased it, and cannot copy the purchase record to another player/save.

Rejected/stale/failed-save purchases leave cash, current equipment, receipt state and mission/cargo unchanged. Save/reload/retry cannot count one payment twice or unlock a tier without a completed transaction.

Explicitly distinguish purchase receipts from salvage/reward/grant ownership and component-grade promotion. Merely fitting found high-grade equipment or achieving numeric promotion must not fabricate paid receipts for skipped levels.

This rule governs shop purchases. Preserve the existing user-authorized immediate fitting of compatible recovered items, earned stat promotion, mission rewards and XYZZY maximum grants as separate provenance-aware acquisition paths. If a later user instruction requires paid prerequisites for those paths too, extend the rule explicitly rather than silently blocking them now.

Migrate existing saves without stripping modules or charging retroactively. Legacy saves lack purchase history, so record an explicit grandfathered prerequisite entitlement for their existing progression, not fictional paid receipts. Keep earned/XYZZY provenance distinct where known; explain legacy normalization in docs. New acquisitions use real receipts.

presentation.equip_ship: All future-level module rows remain visible, with LOCKED - BUY <previous module> and the selected-row explanation of the chain. Price/technology/cash can still be shown but must not hide the prerequisite. Base rows use Standard/Fitted as applicable. Preserve small fixed font, aligned prices, all rows scrollable and accessible by keyboard/pointer.
presentation.commander_and_inventory: Show actual installed/held modules and component-grade progress separately from purchase progression. Where useful, show highest unlocked purchasable step and next required module without claiming inherited capabilities were separately bought.
presentation.voice_and_docs: Purchase refusal displays and voices the exact missing prerequisite once. README, equipment, targeting, navigation, energy, shield, salvage and PLUGH guides and in-game help explain sequential purchases across every module family, with examples and separate standard/earned/recovered/XYZZY/legacy paths.

ownership.Elite Coder 1: Own shared prerequisite graph/receipt/purchase validator, save migration, all shop/fit adapters, UI/docs/voice and integration. Audit every module family; coordinate mission reward/grant provenance with mission owner.
ownership.Elite Coder 2: Recovered module/effect data and provenance contracts plus independent graph/boundary tests. Do not mark recovered/rolled high-grade items as paid receipts or bypass the central purchase validator.
ownership.Mission researcher: Review reward/grant/legacy provenance and exactly-once purchase-event compatibility at a natural checkpoint; no duplicate general implementation.

acceptance: Fresh Basic shield cannot buy Advanced II: each predecessor must be purchased in sequence. Intermediate navigation/energy is required before Advanced; targeting core modules cannot skip earlier modules.
Every other add-on family and shop entry has an explicit valid prerequisite or declared first/base/repeatable relationship; no UI-only rule and no PLUGH/discount/pointer/keyboard bypass.

Purchasing/fitting/removing/selling/upgrading modules preserves separate actual ownership, paid receipt history and numeric promotion. Recovered and mission/XYZZY modules never fabricate paid predecessors.
Legacy saves keep equipment/strength/cash/routes/missions via explicit grandfathering. New receipt state survives save/load/failure/retry without duplicates or unpaid unlocks.
Prerequisite graph is acyclic, family-scoped and stable-ID based, with aliases normalized before validation. Missing/future/duplicate identifiers fail validation rather than unlock arbitrary modules.
All screens/docs/voice report consistent locks and next prerequisites. Focused cross-family/alternate-shop/persistence tests and final integrated make ci gates pass.
